heading: CHAPTER XXV.
title: WHAT FORTUNE CAN EFFECT IN HUMAN AFFAIRS AND HOW TO WITHSTAND HER
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 25 rejects total fatalism without denying contingency. Fortune governs perhaps half of action, but human beings retain a large share through preparation and response.

The chapter operates through two linked models: structural resistance, figured by barriers against a raging river, and strategic adaptation, figured by changing methods so they accord with the spirit of the times.
Julius II is not treated as a universal model of boldness. He succeeds because impetuosity matches his moment. The chapter's danger is fixed character in a changeful world.
